claude_subagent.description: Claude Code workflow subagent (strongest Claude model in the session, effort high). Runs many packages in parallel inside workflows/build_dag.js, no quota problem observed. Reviewer agents are the same model family, so reviewer and implementer share blind spots. Last resort of the engine chain (after local Qwen): never quota-probed, always available.

agy_claude_opus.description: OFF BY DEFAULT since 2026-10-24: Google's Antigravity FAQ does not support wrapping agy inside third-party coding agents on consumer plans (account suspension risk); use agy_manual instead, or re-enable per call with --available agy_claude_opus=yes and an explicit build_dag engineChain at your own risk. agy CLI on the newest Claude Opus that `agy models` lists ("auto:claude-opus", effort suffix in the id). Observed: ~11 min per package, ~2 confirmed defects, but quota exhausts after ~2 runs and stalls ~90 minutes. Same family as the Claude reviewers. Shares one Claude quota bucket with every other agy Claude engine (state file key agy_claude).

agy_gemini_pro.description: OFF BY DEFAULT since 2026-10-24: Google's Antigravity FAQ does not support wrapping agy inside third-party coding agents on consumer plans (account suspension risk); use agy_manual instead, or re-enable per call with --available agy_gemini_pro=yes and an explicit build_dag engineChain at your own risk. agy CLI on the newest Gemini that `agy models` lists ("auto:gemini", resolved per probe/run; the key name predates the Pro retirement on 2026-10-16). Track record below is from gemini-3.1-pro-high: Observed: ~6 min per package, each package tends to need one fix round with 4-9 confirmed defects (spec-literal misses: missing validators, stubbed functions, weakened tests). Different model family from the reviewers, so its errors get caught rather than shared.

agy_manual.description: agy run BY THE USER, not by jbr: Google's Antigravity FAQ (2026-10) says wrapping agy inside third-party coding agents is not supported on consumer plans. `jbr handoff <WP>` writes the packet and prints the line to paste into an agy session you start yourself (pick the model there); `jbr done <WP>` records the outcome; review_level.js reviews it. Never probed, never in an automatic chain or a Jev pick: only an explicit `jbr assign WP=agy_manual` (or a build_dag.js routing pin) hands work to it, and build_dag.js then stops at the handoff instead of falling back.
agy_manual.model: chosen in agy by the user

codex_astra.description: OpenAI Codex CLI on gpt-6-astra, effort high, can spawn its own subagents. Usage limits hit easily; third model family, useful diversity for review-heavy or late packages. 2026-10-14 (Windows): the workspace-write shell failed with "CryptUnprotectData failed" (DPAPI); windows_sandbox danger-full-access fixed it.

ollama_qwen.description: Local Qwen 3.8 27B (MLX) on Ollama, driven by the Codex CLI (--oss). Free, private, never quota-limited; only where Ollama runs (the Mac; elsewhere its probe fails and the chain skips it). Slow: codex sends ~140k tokens of context, so even a trivial package takes several minutes, and a 27B model is weaker than the cloud engines on multi-file work. In the chain after Codex and before the Claude subagent, so it takes work before Claude quota is spent; best for small, fully specified packages. Runners wait up to ~140 min for it.

lan_qwen.description: Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (IQ2_XS 2-bit quant, 32K context) on a LAN OpenAI-compatible server (Responses API), driven by the Codex CLI through a slim CODEX_HOME (~/.codex-local: provider only, no plugins/skills/MCP, so codex's base prompt is ~9K tokens instead of ~108K). Free, never quota-limited; needs LOCAL_LLM_KEY and the server up (otherwise its probe fails and the chain skips it). 2026-10-21: 'say hi' round trip 12 s; benchmark package (two pure text helpers, 8 numbered behaviours, slugify with accent stripping) done in 2.3 min, exit 0, its 9 tests green and 10/10 independent spec checks passed, zero defects. One small package only: no evidence yet on multi-file work. A 2-bit model with ~23K usable tokens: only small, fully specified, low-risk packages. Fourth model family, so the Claude reviewers catch its errors.

muse_spark.description: Meta Muse Code CLI (`muse exec`, headless use documented by Meta for scripts/CI) on Muse Spark 1.3, contributor tier: Meta may use what it is sent (the package's code) to train its models, so ONLY for code you are fine sharing, never private repos. ASSIGN ONLY: never in an automatic chain, `pick` or Jev; only `jbr assign WP=muse_spark` hands work to it. Needs billing set up at dev.meta.ai: on 2026-10-24 this account got `API error 402 Billing verification failed` even on the contributor model (no subscription). Runs with approvals off and the OS sandbox on; personal rules/skills from other agents are not loaded. Quality unproven (no independent benchmark yet): review strictly. Non-training variant: model muse-spark-1.3 with contributor_mode off (paid).
